{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011Ce9R39BQQT3zxdTGnBhko","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've found and fixed the bug.\n\n## What was wrong\n\nThe symptom in the two captures: a screen full of colored cells, and after the window is occluded and brought back to the front (a full repaint), every custom cell color reverts to the default background — **except** the one styled by a CSS *class* (`flagged`, orange), which keeps its color.\n\nThe cause is in `Stylesheet.apply()` (`src/textual/css/stylesheet.py`), the **cache key** used to reuse computed CSS rules across similar-looking nodes during a batch stylesheet application (which is what a repaint/refresh triggers, via `update_nodes`):\n\n```python\ntype(node._parent),                                    # too weak: loses the parent's own id/classes\n(None if node._id is None\n else (node._id if f\"#{node._id}\" not in rules_map else None)),   # drops the id exactly when it matters\n```\n\nThe `_id` branch is inverted. When an `#id` selector targets a node, its id is precisely what distinguishes it from its siblings — but the code replaced the id with `None` in that case, so two id-styled siblings (e.g. `#four` and `#one`) collapse to the **same** cache entry. The first one computed wins; the rest inherit its rules and lose their own color. Cells styled by a **class** carry a distinct `node.classes` in the key, so they land in their own bucket and survive — which is why only `flagged` kept its look. Keying the parent on `type(...)` instead of the parent object compounds it by merging nodes across different parents.\n\nI verified the collapse directly (`#four` rendered teal instead of red), reproduced the full \"lost after repaint\" behavior end-to-end with Textual's headless Pilot on the pre-fix code (`off` and `pinned` lost their colors, `flagged` survived), and confirmed the fix keeps all colors stable.\n\n## The fix\n\nRestore a correct, sufficient cache key — the parent object identity plus the node's own selector-relevant attributes:\n\n```python\ncache_key = (\n    node._parent,\n    node._id,\n    node.classes,\n    node._pseudo_classes_cache_key,\n    node._css_type_name,\n)\n```\n\nThis keeps nodes with different ids in separate cache entries (correctness) while still letting genuinely-identical siblings share (the intended optimization). All 9 runnable stylesheet unit tests pass.\n\nNote: I couldn't run the full `pytest` suite — the environment has no pytest and no network to install it — so I validated by executing the stylesheet tests directly (via a small pytest shim) and with headless-app reproductions. If you'd like, I can add a regression test for this cache-key collapse."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1004,"cache_read_input_tokens":80511,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":1004,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d6f0c084-bd1b-4974-87f3-5e744a81f4f9","uuid":"ff549b1f-88d5-406e-a744-13a3adcb0960","timestamp":"2026-08-18T02:21:08.522Z"}
